questions.question: The speed of a boat when travelling downstream is 48 km/h, whereas when travelling upstream it is 32 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Downstream speed = 48 km/h

Upstream speed = 32 km/h

**Concept used:**

Downstream speed = U + V

Upstream speed = U - V

Where, U = speed of a boat in still water, V = speed of the stream

**Calculation:**

Downstream speed = 48 km/h

⇒ U + V = 48

⇒ V = 48 - U ---(1)

Upstream speed = 32 km/h

⇒ U - V = 32 ---(2)

Substituting the value of V in equation (2),

⇒ U - (48 - U) = 32

⇒ U - 48 + U = 32

⇒ 2U = 32 + 48

⇒ U = 80/2 = 40 km/h

**∴ The speed of the boat in still water**** is 40 km/h.**

questions.question: △ABC ∼ △ LMN and their perimeters are 72 cm and 48 cm, respectively. If LM = 8 cm, then what is the length of AB (in cm)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

△ABC ∼ △ L MN

Perimeter of △ABC = 72 cm

Perimeter of △LMN = 48 cm

LM = 8 cm

**Formula used:**

Perimeter of 1st triangle/Perimeter of 2ⁿd triangle = side of 1st triangle/side of 2ⁿd triangle

**Calculation:**

Let AB = X cm

Side of △ABC/side of △LMN = Perimeter of △ABC/Perimeter of △LMN

⇒ X/8 = 72/48

⇒ X = (72 ×8)/48 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

questions.question: Maya completes (7)/(10) of a work in 15 days and then she completes the remaining work with the help of Suresh in 4 days. In how many days can Maya and Suresh complete the whole work?

Total work = efficiency × time

Together (Maya + Suresh) complete a work = (4 × 10)/3 = 40/3 days

questions.question: 10 men can complete a work in 12 days, and 10 women can complete the same work in 6 days. How many days will it take to complete the work if they work together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

10 men can complete a work = 12 days

10 women can complete the same work = 6 days

**Formula used:**

Total work = efficiency × time

M1 × D1 = M2 × D2

Where, M1 = M2 = Number of workers,

D1 = D2 = Days to complete the work

**Calculation:**

⇒ 10M × 12 = 10W × 6

⇒ M/W = 1/2

Total work = (10 × 1) × 12 = 120

Time taken to complete the work together = 120/(3 × 10) = 4 days

**∴ It will take 4 days to complete the work if they work together.**

questions.question: For what value of q does the system of equations 38x + qy + 171 = 0 and 46x + 414y + 207 = 0 have infinite number of solutions?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1st equation = 38x + qy + 171 = 0

2nd equation = 46x + 414y + 207 = 0

**Concept used:**

If an equation has infinite number of solutions then

a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 ; a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0

⇒ a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2

**Calculation:**

⇒ a1/a2 = b1/b2 

⇒ 38/46 = q/414

⇒ q = (38 × 414)/46

⇒ q = 38 × 9 = 342

**∴ The correct answer is 342.**

questions.question: Raman buys 18 kg of rice at ₹35 per kg and 30 kg of rice at ₹39 per kg. Find the average price (in ₹) per kg of the total rice.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate of 18 kg rice = 35 Rs/kg

Rate of 30 kg rice = 39 Rs/kg

**Formula used:**

Average price = total price/total quantity

**Calculation:**

Total price of rice = (18 × 35) + (30 × 39) = Rs.1800

Total quantity = 18 + 30 = 48 kg

Average price = total price/total quantity

⇒ 1800/48 = 37.5 Rs/kg

** ∴ The average price (in ₹) per kg is 37.5 Rs/kg.**

questions.question:
Find the fourth proportion of the following numbers.

(1)/(3) of 6, (4)/(5) of 15, (3)/(7) of 21.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1st number = (1/3) × 6 = 2

2ⁿd number = (4/5) × 15 = 12

3rd number = (3/7) × 21 = 9

**Concept used:**

1st number : 2nd number : : 3rd number : 4th number

4th proportional = (3rd number × 2nd number)/1st number

**Calculation:**

Let 4th number = x

1st number : 2nd number : : 3rd number : 4th number

⇒ 2 : 12 : : 9 : x

⇒ x = (9 × 12)/2

⇒ x = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

questions.question:
A trader offers to sell a commodity under any of the two schemes mentioned below:

Scheme 1: The trader offers two successive discounts of 20% and 12.5% on the sale of each unit.

Scheme 2: The trader offers the buyer an option to ‘pay for y units, get z units free’. The buyer realizes that if he needs to buy (y + z) units, it does not matter to him which of the two schemes he opts for.

Which of the following options gives a correct ordered pair of (y, z)?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Effective discount = D₁% + D₂% - (D₁% × D₂%)/100

**Calculation:**

Scheme 1:

Effective discount% = 20 + 12.5 - (20 × 12.5)/100

⇒ 32.5 - 2.5 = 30%

Scheme 2:

⇒ (z × 100)/(y + z) = 30%

We need to check it by option:

If we put y = 3 ; z = 7 then

⇒ (7 × 100)/(10) ≠ 30%

If we put y = 7 ; z = 10 then

⇒ (10 × 100)/(17) ≠ 30%

If we put y = 10 ; z = 7 then

⇒ (7 × 100)/(17) ≠ 30%

If we put y = 7 ; z = 3 then

So the value of y = 7 & z = 3 satisfies the equation.

questions.question: What is the least value of * so that the number 457643*4 is divisible by 18?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number = 457643*4

**Concept used:**

Divisibility Rule of 9:

if the sum of the digits of the number is divisible by 9, then the number is divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 2:

A number whose last digit is an even number i.e. 2, 4, 6, 8 including 0, the number is divisible by 2.

**Calculation:**

18 = 2 × 9

If a number is a multiple of both 2 and 9, then the number is also a multiple of 18.

Number = 457643*4

The last digit of the number = 4

4 is an even number and a multiple of 2. Hence the number is divisible by 2.

The sum of the digits = 4 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 4 + 3 + * + 4 = 33 + *

The least possible value of * is = 3

**∴ The correct option is 2. **

questions.question: The marked price of a commodity was given as ₹y per kg. After two successive discounts of 8% and 12.5%, respectively, the retailer purchased it for ₹3,059 per kg. What was the value of y?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price (M.P) = y Rs./kg

Discount (D₁) = 8% ; Discount (D₂) = 12.5%

Selling price (S.P) = Rs.3059 Rs./kg

**Concept used:**

Effective discount = D1 + D2 - (D1 × D2)/100

Selling price (S.P) = M.P × (100 - D)%

**Calculation:**

Effective discount = D1 + D2 - (D1 × D2)/100

⇒ 8 + 12.5 - (8 × 12.5)/100

⇒ 20.5 - 1 = 19.5%

⇒ M.P × (100 - D)% = S.P

⇒ y × (100 - 19.5)% = 3059

⇒ y × 80.5% = 3059

⇒ y = (3059 × 100)/80.5 = 38 × 100 = Rs.3800 

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.3800. **

questions.question: A shopkeeper keeps the marked price of his goods 50% more than the cost price. If he gives successive discounts of 5%, 10% and 20% on marked price, then what is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked up price % = 50%

Discount (D₁) = 5% ; discount (D₂) = 10% ; discount (D₃) = 20%

**Formula used:**

Profit (P) = (SP - CP)

Profit% = (P × 100)/CP

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost price (CP) = Rs.100

Marked price (MP) = 100 × 150% = 150

After the first discount (D1) = 150 × (100 - 5)% = 150 × 95%

⇒ Rs.142.5

The 2nd discount (D2) = 142.5 × (100 - 10)% = 142.5 × 90%

⇒ Rs.128.25

After the 3rd discount (D3) = 128.25 × (100 - 20)%

⇒ 128.25 × 80% = Rs.102.6

Sot the selling price (S.P) = Rs.102.6

Profit (P) = (S.P - C.P)

⇒ (102.6 - 100) = Rs.2.6

Profit% = (P × 100)/C.P

⇒ (2.6 × 100)/100 

⇒ 26/10 = 13/5 = 2(3)/(5)%

**∴ The profit percentage**** is 2(3)/(5)%.**

questions.question: On reducing the entry fee by 25% in a museum, the number of people coming to the museum increased by 50%, Find the percentage increase or decrease in the collection of the entry fee.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The entry fee for the museum is reduced by 25%.

The number of people coming to the museum is increased by 50%.

**Calculation:**

Original entry fee : reduced entry fee = 100 : 75 = 4 : 3

Number of people before reduction of entry fee : Number of people after reduction of entry fee

⇒ 100 : 150 = 2 : 3

Revenue of museum before reduction of fee : Revenue of museum after reduction of fee

⇒ 4 × 2 : 3 × 3 = 8 : 9

% increment = {(9 - 8) × 100}/8

⇒ {1 × 100}/8 = 12.5%

**∴ Percentage increase in the collection of the entry fee is 12.5%.**
